name: Enterprise spatial computing
summary: Headsets and spatial interfaces overlay or simulate information for training, design, inspection and remote assistance.
useCase: A trainee practices a rare maintenance procedure in a simulated environment, while an expert reviews the same three-dimensional equipment model.
whyNow: Hardware and software continue improving, but commercial adoption has been uneven and attention has shifted toward lighter glasses. Meta’s Reality Labs revenue was US$1.90 billion in 2023 and US$2.21 billion in 2025, a modest result compared with the scale of investment. That consumer-heavy segment is an imperfect proxy for enterprise demand. The credible opportunity is concentrated in tasks where spatial understanding changes the outcome.

mainstream.scope: Routine use in selected high-value enterprise training, design review, simulation and frontline assistance workflows.
mainstream.rationale: Specialist use cases already have working products, but comfort, content production and recurring value still limit wider rollout. The estimate is conditional on practical hardware and sustained deployment economics. A downside case remains niche beyond 2035; the forecast does not assume office workers universally replace monitors or meetings with headsets.

direction: Selective growth; broad headset adoption remains uneven

metric.name: Meta Reality Labs revenue — adjacent hardware/platform proxy
metric.scope: Meta’s Reality Labs segment, including consumer AR/VR hardware, software and other products.
metric.limitations: Predominantly a consumer-platform measure, not enterprise spatial-computing adoption. Product mix shifts toward wearables complicate interpretation. Modest segment growth does not establish headset shipment growth or profitable business models. No invented 2026 annual result is included.
metric.futureNote: No comparable enterprise adoption forecast is sufficiently robust to plot as measured growth. The forward path is conditional and may remain below mainstream beyond 2035.

maturity.note: Analyst ordinal assessment, not an adoption percentage: 0 research, 1 proof of concept, 2 pilots, 3 commercial niche, 4 routine use in the stated market, 5 established/expanding. Future values are a scenario.

milestones.text: No comparable enterprise spatial-computing adoption census identified.
No same-scope annual enterprise deployment measurement supplied.
Meta Reality Labs revenue was US$1.896 billion, an adjacent consumer-heavy market signal.
Apple’s Vision Pro became available in the U.S.; Reality Labs revenue was US$2.146 billion.
Reality Labs revenue reached US$2.207 billion, with the product mix extending beyond VR headsets.
Meta’s filing emphasized a planned spending mix favoring wearables; specialist enterprise simulation and glasses vendors remained active.

tailwinds: Training dangerous or rare procedures can justify specialized immersive systems.
Spatial visualization can improve design review and frontline assistance when two-dimensional instructions are inadequate.
bottlenecks: Comfort, battery life, visual quality and social acceptance limit session length and repeated use.
Content creation, fleet support and weak repeat usage can overwhelm hardware savings.
watchMetrics: Monthly active deployed headsets/glasses and hours of productive use per device.
Training retention, error reduction and time saved, net of content and device-management costs.
